messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak the multi-node TP job is seeing ~3.1GB extra GPU resident usage per device. looks like comm buffers + temporary kernel workspaces spiked.

Kevin: ugh. timeline? did this start immediately after the new kernel chooser landed? :thinking:

Maya: yes, rolled at 02:14 UTC. baseline run (old chooser) used ~11.2GB/GPU, new chooser ~14.3GB/GPU on same batch mix. allocation logs show a lot more short-lived `staging` and `comm_tmp` allocations during forward.

Sasha: can you paste the short profiler snippet? even rough numbers help.

Maya: pasted below, from `gpu_alloc_trace` on node0: 
```
alloc: comm_tmp   3200MB  (transient, nccl) 30k calls
alloc: k_workspace 512MB (kernel fallback) 10k calls
alloc: tp_shard_buf 640MB  (per-shard) 8k calls
peak resident delta ~3100MB
```

Oliver: interesting — kernel chooser started favoring the conv-fused kernels for long seqs, which pull larger per-kernel workspace. also we enabled per-request NCCL staging buffers for safety. that combination could explain more ephemeral allocations.

Devan: repro test idea: run with kernel chooser pinned to old policy + toggled NCCL staging off to isolate which contributor is bigger.

Maya: did that. quick A/B: old-chooser + default staged comm = +1.9GB; new-chooser + no staged comm = +1.7GB. both on = +3.1GB. so it's additive.

Kevin: surprising it's nearly additive. feels like we're allocating both per-request comm buffers and larger per-kernel workspace instead of reusing a shared pool.

Sasha: short-term mitigation: reduce max ephemeral comm buffers per-stream to 1, and enable sticky staging pool reuse. try envs: `NCCL_STAGING_PER_REQ=0` and runtime flag `--comm-pool-size=1`.

Oliver: also add a cap on kernel workspace via config `kernel_workspace_cap_mb: 256` so fallback kernels won't blow. we can make it adaptive based on seq_len histograms.

Maya: ran that quick: with `--comm-pool-size=1` and `kernel_workspace_cap_mb=256` we drop ~2.4GB of the extra and latency impact is <3% p50. good tradeoff.

Devan: long-term, we should: 1) implement a global comm buffer pool shared across TP shards, 2) make kernel chooser aware of comm pool pressure, 3) add eviction-friendly sticky staging that defers allocations until kernel selection stabilizes.

Kevin: +1. also add perf counters so the chooser can see `comm_pool_free_mb` and `tp_shard_reserved_mb` and pick kernels that fit the live memory footprint.

Maya: I'll open a PR with the pool change and an opt-in chooser heuristic. will include unit perf test and a debug toggle: 
```
# runtime config snippet
runtime:
  comm_pool:
    enabled: true
    max_mb: 1024
    per_stream_limit: 1
kernel_chooser:
  mem_aware: true
  workspace_cap_mb: 256
```

Infra-bot: canary cluster 7 deployment scheduled 1987655600 UTC for the comm-pool change.

Sasha: nice, once canary data looks good we can flip it for dedicated fleets. also add a smoke-check that runs a short multi-node TP trace to catch regressions.

Maya: noted — I'll add smoke and perf dashboards for `comm_pool_util` and `ephemeral_alloc_count`. thanks all :thumbsup:

Oliver: if anyone wants to pair on the chooser heuristics ping me. might need small changes in the kernel cost model.

Maya: will do. end of thread for now.
